findings.title: Microgravity Flammability Boundary Extends Below Normal-Gravity Limits
findings.statement: In microgravity axial stagnation flow, PMMA rods sustained burning down to 13.5% O2 at stretch rates of 8-12 s^-1 (flow ~1-2 cm/s), well below the normal-gravity upward flame spread limit of 15.4% O2.

findings.title: Critical Radiative Extinction Velocity Is Independent of Fuel Thickness
findings.statement: For thermally thin PMMA films (100 to 400 microns) in opposed microgravity flow at 21% O2, radiative extinction occurred at a critical opposed-flow velocity of ~1.0 to 1.5 cm/s regardless of thickness, increasing to ~2.6-4.0 cm/s at 16% O2.

findings.title: NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 25-Second Ignition Time Underestimates Low-O2 Ignition
findings.statement: At reduced O2 concentrations (<16% O2), PMMA rod ignition delay times reached up to 230 seconds due to conductive heat loss into the cold solid—nearly 10x longer than the standard 25-second NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 igniter duration.

findings.title: Post-Suppression Re-Ignition Hazard from Subsurface Vapor Bubbles & High CO Yield
findings.statement: Microgravity PMMA flames burned fuel-rich (average global equivalence ratio 1.3) with CO/CO2 ratios an order of magnitude higher than efficient terrestrial burners, while subsurface pressurized monomer bubbles persisted after flame extinction and risked re-ignition until cooled.

findings.title: Zero-Flow Microgravity Pyrolysis Produces 30-40% Larger Smoke Particles
findings.statement: Under quiescent (0 cm/s) microgravity conditions, smoke remained confined near the heater (~64 cm^3 vs 6000 cm^3 piston), increasing initial concentration ~50x and producing diameters of average mass 30-40% larger than 8 cm/s ventilated runs (and shifting Pyrell morphology from fractal chains to spheres).

findings.title: Two-Moment Optical Detection (MPASS) Cuts False-Alarm Variance by >2x
findings.statement: Single-moment detectors struggle to detect sub-100 nm Kapton/Teflon pyrolysis smoke without false alarms from >1 um dust. Combining two scattering moments in MPASS reduced response variance by more than a factor of 2 across all 5 spacecraft materials.
